newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks power higher, boosted by bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks power higher, boosted by bonds.

text.p: U.S. stocks scrambled higher on Wednesday, driven by a robust bond market, optimism about the inflation and interest rate outlook and some residual benefit from the proposed U.S. balanced budget deal.
The Dow Jones Industrial average rallied 85 points, or about one percent, to 8259, after the New York Stock Exchange set curbs on index-arbitrage trading.
The Nasdaq composite rose 12 points to 1584 and the long bond soared 27/32 to yield 6.33 percent.
Stocks and bonds got an early lift from new home sales data for June and May, analysts said.

The U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes, seasonally adjusted, rose 6.1 percent to a 819,000 annual rate. But analysts pointed to a more striking downward revision to the May data, which was now showed sales rose one percent instead of the previous 7.1 percent gain.

"That is a big revision," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. He said financial markets were also boosted by the budget deal, lower rates, a strong dollar and a dwindling supply of government debt offerings.
